newsitem.title: UK: UK leisure group Rank says outlook promising.
newsitem.headline: UK leisure group Rank says outlook promising.

text.p: British leisure company Rank Group Plc, in the process of focusing on core businesses, said on Thursday that the outlook was "promising" as it reported full-year results badly hit by exceptional charges.

"The steps we have taken are already making the company more focused, entrepreneurial and forward looking," chief executive Andrew Teare said. "These changes, together with the benefits of our investment programme and the generally favourable economic climate provide a promising outlook for Rank."
Rank, owner of the Hard Rock Cafe brand, said that 1996 pre-tax profit fell to 65 million pounds ($105.1 million) from 515 million in 1995.

The 1996 figure was hit by exceptional charges of 232 million pounds, mainly caused by property write-offs, loss on disposals and restructuring charges. The 1995 figure had been flattered by an exceptional gain of 236 million.

Rank increased its net dividend by eight percent to 17 pence per share while operating profits before exceptional items rose 13 percent to 290 million pounds. Turnover was up nine percent at 2.08 billion pounds.
Rank said on Thursday that it planned to create 3,000 full-time jobs in Britain this year as it opened a number of new holiday and leisure centres, pub-restaurants and bingo clubs.
